skill.name: browsing-with-playwright
skill.description: Automate browser tasks through a local Playwright MCP server, including navigation, screenshots, form filling, element interaction, and page data extraction.
skill.summary: Control a browser with Playwright MCP for web testing, form workflows, screenshots, and structured page extraction.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, JSON Schema URLs, generated reference documentation, or fixed health-check commands. Real risks remain because the skill can launch a user-supplied stdio MCP command, send MCP requests to configured endpoints, manage local processes through /tmp PID files, and execute arbitrary Playwright code in a shared browser context.

remediation.issue: Stdio MCP transport executes a user-supplied command with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Parse stdio commands into an argument list and run subprocess.Popen with shell=False, or remove stdio support if this skill only needs local Playwright HTTP MCP.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts use predictable /tmp PID files for process control.
remediation.suggestion: Store PID files in a user-owned runtime directory with restrictive permissions, validate PID contents as digits, and quote command substitutions consistently.

remediation.issue: browser_run_code can execute arbitrary Playwright code in a shared browser context.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to run browser code from untrusted prompts and recommend closing the browser or using an isolated context after sensitive sessions.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary browser code execution capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to call browser_run_code with supplied Playwright code. This is a powerful browser automation feature that can read page content and act in the active shared browser context if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow explicitly passes a code string to browser_run_code. The risk is contextual because trusted users may need it, but untrusted prompts could abuse it.

semantic_findings.title: Shared browser context may expose session state
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires --shared-browser-context so browser state persists across MCP client calls. Persistent session state can expose authenticated pages or cookies during later browser automation tasks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation clearly requires a shared browser context and advises keeping the server running for long sessions. This creates a real privacy boundary concern, although it is not inherently malicious.

content.value_statement: Manual browser testing and data collection can be slow and hard to repeat. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a local Playwright MCP workflow for controlled browser actions.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops a local Playwright MCP server on a configurable port.
Calls MCP browser tools for navigation, clicks, typing, form filling, and option selection.
Captures screenshots and accessibility snapshots for page inspection.
Runs browser_evaluate and browser_run_code for custom page extraction or multi-step workflows.
Lists MCP tools and emits tool reference documentation through the bundled MCP client.
limitations: Requires Node, npx, Python 3, and the Playwright MCP package to be available locally.
Browser actions depend on the current page state and element references from snapshots.
Shared browser context can retain login state across calls until the browser is closed.
It is not intended for static content fetching when curl or wget is enough.

use_cases.title: Test a web form end to end
use_cases.description: Navigate to a page, fill fields, submit the form, wait for confirmation, and capture proof with a screenshot.

use_cases.title: Inspect a browser-only workflow
use_cases.description: Use snapshots, clicks, waits, and screenshots to understand dynamic pages that need JavaScript execution.

use_cases.title: Extract visible page data
use_cases.description: Open a page, collect text through snapshots or browser evaluation, and summarize the result for a research task.

prompt_templates.title: Open a page and report what is visible
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Playwright browser skill to open the page I provide. Take a snapshot, summarize the visible sections, and tell me if the page loaded correctly.

prompt_templates.title: Fill and submit a simple form
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Playwright MCP server, open this form, fill the fields with the values I provide, submit it, and capture the confirmation screen.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a dynamic UI state
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser snapshots and screenshots to reproduce this UI issue. Click through the stated steps, wait for each state change, and report the observed behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Run a multi-step extraction workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright MCP to navigate through the target pages, run safe page evaluation for the requested data, and return a concise table of findings with source pages.

output_examples.input: Check whether the signup page loads and has email and password fields.
output_examples.output: The page loaded successfully. The snapshot shows email and password fields, a submit button, and a terms checkbox. A screenshot was captured for review.

output_examples.input: Submit the contact form with the test values and confirm the result.
output_examples.output: The form was filled and submitted. The page displayed a success message, and the final screen was saved as evidence.

output_examples.input: Extract the visible product names from the catalog page.
output: Captured the page state after loading.
Returned the visible product names and noted items hidden behind pagination.

best_practices: Take a fresh browser_snapshot before clicking or typing so element references are current.
Stop the Playwright MCP server when browser work is complete, especially after authenticated sessions.
Use browser_run_code only for trusted workflows and prefer targeted tool calls for simple actions.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for static downloads when a direct HTTP fetch is sufficient.
Do not reuse a shared browser context for unrelated users or sensitive accounts.
Do not run Playwright code copied from untrusted pages, prompts, or tickets.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, clicks, typing, form filling, screenshots, waits, and page extraction through Playwright MCP.

faq.question: Does it need a local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script starts a local Playwright MCP server, and the Python client sends MCP requests to it.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude Code, Claude, and Codex as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it browse authenticated sites?
faq.answer: Yes, if the browser session is authenticated. Users should close the browser after sensitive work.

faq.question: Is browser_run_code safe?
faq.answer: It is powerful and should be used only with trusted code. Prefer specific browser tools when possible.

faq.question: What should I do if the server stops responding?
faq.answer: Stop and restart the local MCP server, then take a new snapshot before continuing browser actions.
